root_cause.text: The scatterlist length field, defined as an unsigned int, was not being constrained to respect the max_segment limit when accumulating pages from folios, allowing the length to overflow when a single scatterlist entry accumulated 4GB or more of pages.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds two critical constraints: (1) it limits `nr_pages` during initial allocation using `min_array()` to include `max_segment / PAGE_SIZE` as a constraint, and (2) it adds a check when appending to an existing scatterlist entry to ensure `(max_segment - sg->length) / PAGE_SIZE` is not exceeded. The original code had a comment `/* XXX: could overflow? */` acknowledging the risk but failing to implement the necessary bounds checking. The vulnerability was introduced in commit 0b62af28f249b when the code was converted to use folio_batch, which processes larger page allocations that can more easily trigger the 4GB overflow condition on the unsigned int length field.

vuln_statements.content: nr_pages = min_t(unsigned long, folio_nr_pages(folio), page_count - i);

intent_record.intent_summary: Add max_segment size constraint to nr_pages calculation to prevent scatter-gather table entries from exceeding hardware segment limits.
intent_record.what: Replaced a min_t() call comparing two values (folio_nr_pages(folio) and page_count - i) with a min_array() call that compares three values: folio_nr_pages(folio), page_count - i, and max_segment / PAGE_SIZE.
intent_record.how: The original code computed the minimum of the folio's page count and remaining pages to allocate. The new code adds a third constraint: the maximum segment size divided by PAGE_SIZE. This ensures nr_pages never exceeds the hardware's max_segment limit, preventing potential buffer overruns or DMA violations when building scatter-gather tables.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential sg->length overflow by clamping nr_pages to the remaining segment capacity before accumulating into sg->length.
intent_record.what: Replaced a comment 'XXX: could overflow?' with an actual bounds check that limits nr_pages to the remaining space in the current segment using min_t(), and added a blank line after the assignment.
intent_record.how: This change prevents potential buffer overflow by capping nr_pages to fit within max_segment constraints before adding to sg->length. Previously, the code had a TODO comment acknowledging the overflow risk but did nothing to prevent it. Now it actively enforces that sg->length cannot exceed max_segment by calculating the maximum safe nr_pages value.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 26a8e32e6d77900819c0c730fbfb393692dbbeea
Author: Matthew Wilcox (Oracle) <willy@infradead.org>
Date:   Tue Sep 19 20:48:55 2023 +0100

    i915: Limit the length of an sg list to the requested length
    
    The folio conversion changed the behaviour of shmem_sg_alloc_table() to
    put the entire length of the last folio into the sg list, even if the sg
    list should have been shorter.  gen8_ggtt_insert_entries() relied on the
    list being the right length and would overrun the end
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the fix for the vulnerability. The root cause was that scatterlist length could overflow when accumulating pages from folios without respecting the max_segment limit. The fix is clearly visible in the diff: (1) A new variable `nr_pages` is introduced and constrained using `min_t(unsigned long, folio_nr_pages(folio), page_count - i)` at lines 154-155, which limits the number of pages to not exceed the remaining page count needed. (2) This constrained `nr_pages` is then used instead of the full `folio_nr_pages(folio)` when setting sg_set_folio() at line 163 and when accumulating sg->length at line 166. (3) The loop counter `i` is also updated to use the constrained `nr_pages` at line 169. This prevents the scatterlist length from overflowing by ensuring that the last folio entry is clamped to the requested length rather than using the entire folio size. The vulnerable construct (unconstrained folio_size/folio_nr_pages accumulation) is absent in this version because it has been replaced with the constrained nr_pages calculation.
